Longitudinal Summary

Over the reported periods from Q1 2021 through Q4 2022, the topic of equity primarily centers on equity securities valuations, equity warrant valuations, and related foreign currency impacts, as reflected in the 'Other income (expense), net' line item. Significant valuation gains and losses were recorded related to the equity investment in Rivian Automotive, Inc., including an $11.8 billion gain in 2021 and a subsequent $12.7 billion loss in 2022. Management consistently disclosed the dilutive potential of issuing additional equity or convertible debt securities and highlighted ongoing evaluations of financing and capital structure strategies. Equity-method investment activity showed fluctuations but no forward guidance was provided on these figures. The company also emphasized the use of restricted stock units for employee compensation to align interests with shareholders.

Forecasting Credibility: None

No guidance versus actual pairs were provided for equity-related items, precluding any assessment of management's forecasting credibility on this topic. The disclosures focus on actual reported figures and qualitative commentary without forward-looking quantitative guidance. Therefore, it is not possible to judge forecasting accuracy or reliability from the available data.

Trends

  • Large valuation swings in equity investments
  • Significant gains in 2021 followed by losses in 2022
  • Consistent emphasis on equity securities and warrant valuations
  • Ongoing evaluation of capital structure and financing options
  • Use of restricted stock units for compensation

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • Equity securities valuation volatility
  • Dilution risk from additional equity or convertible debt issuance
  • Foreign currency impacts on other income (expense), net
  • Tax benefits related to equity investment valuation changes

Key Concerns

  • No forward guidance provided on equity-related items limits ability to assess forecasting credibility.
  • Large fluctuations in equity investment valuations, especially related to Rivian, introduce significant volatility in reported results.
  • Potential dilution risk noted but no quantification or forward outlook given.

Conclusion

From an equity perspective, the company experiences substantial volatility driven by marketable equity securities valuations, particularly its investment in Rivian Automotive, Inc. Management provides detailed disclosures on actual valuation gains and losses but does not offer forward guidance on these items, making it impossible to evaluate forecasting accuracy. The firm acknowledges dilution risks and continues to use equity-based compensation aligned with shareholder interests. Investors should be aware of the inherent valuation volatility and lack of predictive guidance in this area when assessing the company's financial outlook.

Okay. Thank you. So Brian, I think you just reported a quarter-on-quarter decline on headcount, which was by design after what happened last quarter, but it won't be too long before you are gearing up for the holidays. So how do you think the environment is going to fair for you to be adding headcount? And also the stock-based compensation came in below, where you had guided for the second quarter. So is this a matter of not hitting the hiring goals you were hoping for, or do you think the environment for the hiring of technical and engineering talent is losing up a little bit? Thanks.Q2 2022complete1Earnings transcripthighsource
Sure, Stephen. Thank you. On the headcount, yes, I think it was more as we mentioned last quarter – last year – excuse me, in Q1, we added – to give you a flavor for it, we added 14,000 workers in Q1, prior year we had reduced our net headcount by 27,000. So we’re pretty transparent about the fact that we had hired a lot of people in Q1 for the coverage of the Omicron variant, luckily that variant subsided and we were left with a higher headcount position that has come down through adjusting our hiring levels and normal attrition and – was pretty much resolved by the end of April or early part of May. So that is dominating the quarter-over-quarter reduction in headcount. I would note that we're still up 188,000 year-over-year and nearly double the headcount of what we had heading into the pandemic in early 2020. So you're right, there will be adjustments to that as we move forward into more holiday level demand. Right now, we see a stabilization in the workforce, maybe we see good hiring rates. And so I think as you remember, there was a very difficult labor period in the second half of last year, and it didn't arrived kind of quickly out of nowhere. So we're certainly diligent on that and making sure we have a good workplace and an environment that will attract employees.Q2 2022complete1Earnings transcripthighsource

See “Note 5 — Acquisitions, Goodwill, and Acquired Intangible Assets.” Other Assets Included in “Other assets” on our consolidated balance sheets are amounts primarily related to video and music content, net of accumulated amortization; long-term deferred tax assets; acquired intangible assets, net of accumulated amortization; equity warrant assets and certain equity investments; and satellite network launch services deposits.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Other Operating Expense (Income), Net Other operating expense (income), net, consists primarily of the amortization of intangible assets and, for 2020, a benefit from accelerated vesting of warrants to acquire equity of a vendor partially offset by a lease impairment and, for 2022, $ 1.1 billion of impairments of property and equipment and operating leases.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Equity investments are accounted for using the equity method of accounting, or at fair value if we elect the fair value option, if the investment gives us the ability to exercise significant influence, but not control, over an investee.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Equity investments in private companies for which we do not have the ability to exercise significant influence are accounted for at cost, with adjustments for observable changes in prices or impairments, and are classified as “Other assets” on our consolidated balance sheets with adjustments recognized in “Other income (expense), net” on our consolidated statements of operations.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
See “Note 7 — Commitments and Contingencies.” (3) Our equity investment in Rivian had a fair value of $ 15.6 billion and $ 2.9 billion as of December 31, 2021 and December 31, 2022, respectively.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Cash, Cash Equivalents, Restricted Cash, and Marketable Securities As of December 31, 2021 and 2022, our cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities primarily consisted of cash, AAA-rated money market funds, U.S. and foreign government and agency securities, other investment grade securities, and marketable equity securities.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
As a result of future acquisitions or mergers, we might need to issue additional equity securities, spend our cash, or incur debt, contingent liabilities, or amortization expenses related to intangible assets, any of which could reduce our profitability and harm our business or only be available on unfavorable terms, if at all.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
The trading price of our common stock fluctuates significantly in response to, among other risks, the risks described elsewhere in this Item 1A, as well as: • changes in interest rates; • conditions or trends in the Internet and the industry segments we operate in; • quarterly variations in operating results; • fluctuations in the stock market in general and market prices for Internet-related companies in particular; • changes in financial estimates by us or decisions to increase or decrease future spending or investment levels; • changes in financial estimates and recommendations by securities analysts; • changes in our capital structure, including issuance of additional debt or equity to the public; • changes in the valuation methodology of, or performance by, other e-commerce or technology companies; and • transactions in our common stock by major investors and certain analyst reports, news, and speculation.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
We also continue to inspect and refine the mechanisms we use to hire, develop, evaluate, and retain our employees to promote equity for all candidates and employees.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities None.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Equity Investment Risk As of December 31, 2022, our recorded value in equity and equity warrant investments in public and private companies was $7.2 billion.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
Our equity and equity warrant investments in publicly traded companies, which primarily relate to Rivian, represent $5.0 billion of our investments as of December 31, 2022, and are recorded at fair value, which is subject to market price volatility.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource
We record our equity warrant investments in private companies at fair value and adjust our equity investments in private companies for observable price changes or impairments.Q4 2022complete1SEC filinghighsource

What was asked

Q — Stephen Ju — Credit Suisse: Okay. Thank you. So Brian, I think you just reported a quarter-on-quarter decline on headcount, which was by design after what happened last quarter, but it won't be too long before you are gearing up for the holidays. So how do you think the environment is going to fair for you to be adding headcount? And also the stock-based compensation came in below, where you had guided for the second quarter. So is this a matter of not hitting the hiring goals you were hoping for, or do you think the environment for the hiring of technical and engineering talent is losing up a little bit? Thanks.
A: Sure, Stephen. Thank you. On the headcount, yes, I think it was more as we mentioned last quarter – last year – excuse me, in Q1, we added – to give you a flavor for it, we added 14,000 workers in Q1, prior year we had reduced our net headcount by 27,000. So we’re pretty transparent about the fact that we had hired a lot of people in Q1 for the coverage of the Omicron variant, luckily that variant subsided and we were left with a higher headcount position that has come down through adjusting our hiring levels and normal attrition and – was pretty much resolved by the end of April or early part of May. So that is dominating the quarter-over-quarter reduction in headcount. I would note that we're still up 188,000 year-over-year and nearly double the headcount of what we had heading into the pandemic in early 2020. So you're right, there will be adjustments to that as we move forward into more holiday level demand. Right now, we see a stabilization in the workforce, maybe we see good hiring rates. And so I think as you remember, there was a very difficult labor period in the second half of last year, and it didn't arrived kind of quickly out of nowhere. So we're certainly diligent on that and making sure we have a good workplace and an environment that will attract employees. And Stephen on your – just to your question on stock-based comp, as you mentioned, we do utilize restricted stock units or RSU as our primary mode of equity compensation. And as we always remind you, employee annual RSU grants do occur in the second quarter. And as a result, we typically see a step-up in the SBC expense from Q1 to Q2 and of course, you saw it this time around. The growth in the line is impacted overall also on the step-up by continued headcount. We've grown our workforce over the last few years. And as Brian talked about hiring in a number of areas of the business, including engineers, other tech workers, and there's some component of the wage inflation as we look to continue to hire and retain employees there. In terms of the coming in at the five – little over $5 billion for stock-based comp, the main driver there was primarily driven by fewer employees stock awards vested – excuse me, fewer employee stock awards we’re vesting in Q2 than we expected. Thanks for joining us on the call today and for your questions. A replay will be available on our Investor Relations website for at least three months. We appreciate your interest in Amazon, and we look forward to talking with you again, next quarter.

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"As a result of future acquisitions or mergers, we might need to issue additional equity securities, spend our cash, or incur debt, contingent liabilities, or amortization expenses related to intangible assets, any of which could reduce our profitability and harm our business or only be available on unfavorable terms, if at all."
  • jump to section"The trading price of our common stock fluctuates significantly in response to, among other risks, the risks described elsewhere in this Item 1A, as well as: • changes in interest rates; • conditions or trends in the Internet and the industry segments we operate in; • quarterly variations in operating results; • fluctuations in the stock market in general and market prices for Internet-related companies in particular; • changes in financial estimates by us or decisions to increase or decrease future spending or investment levels; • changes in financial estimates and recommendations by securities analysts; • changes in our capital structure, including issuance of additional debt or equity to the public; • changes in the valuation methodology of, or performance by, other e-commerce or technology companies; and • transactions in our common stock by major investors and certain analyst reports, news, and speculation."
